subject: ventures/auto-loan-interest-deduction-calculator
professional: an enrolled agent or CPA preparing individual 1040s with Schedule 1-A. First checks: the 163(h)(4) cap and the $200-per-$1,000-or-portion phase-out at $100k/$200k, MFS and joint treatment, every eligibility element (new, US final assembly, first lien, personal use, after 2024-12-31, vehicle type/GVWR), the VIN-on-return requirement, and what counts as qualified interest on a mixed or refinanced loan

evidence.correctness: The shipped calc.mjs was run on 8 probe cases (probe.mjs in the session scratchpad), and the page was driven in headless Chrome over CDP (cdp.mjs). Five outputs were recomputed by hand from IRC 163(h)(4): a $10,000 per-return cap, reduced by $200 per $1,000 or portion of MAGI over $100,000, or $200,000 joint. Joint at $212,500 with $8,000 interest gives 7,400 and 1,628 at 22%. Single at $123,456.78 gives 5,200, with the fractional excess rounded up. MFS at $120,000 gives 6,000. HoH at exactly $100,000 has no reduction. Joint at $249,001 gives 0. The page's worked example ($3,400, $748) and the MFS guide's 6,000/12,000/2,000 example also check by hand. All pass. One input-handling failure: a blank MAGI is read as $0, and the page shows the full deduction with a message that the income is under the phase-out threshold. Caveat: the statute and regulations could not be opened this session (uscode.house.gov, law.cornell.edu, govinfo.gov and federalregister.gov all refused). Thresholds, rounding up, MFS at $100,000 and the per-return cap rest on the auditor's knowledge of the enacted text plus WebSearch summaries of T.D. 10054. Arithmetic right on every hand case, one silent-default trap: 3.
evidence.completeness: Exercised the features the README and page claim to be done: filing status (all four), MAGI, marginal rate, interest, the 8 checkboxes (a test zeroes each one alone and names it), the phase-out and joint/MFS findings, the savings estimate, Load example, Clear, and the opt-out of usage counting (present). The page loaded in headless Chrome from a local server with no exceptions. Load example renders '$3,400 — roughly $748'. Both subpages link back and to each other. served-copy.mjs reports a clean llms.txt, sitemap and canonicals; the source llms.txt has github.io URLs, which the deploy rewrites (source-only, not filed). No TODOs or stubs. Refinancing is honestly listed as not modelled. Everything claimed works: 3.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root gives 41/41 pass. Six mutants were seeded with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py. All five in calc.mjs were caught: ceil to floor, the joint threshold, the cap dropped from min(), the `excess <= 0` boundary, and the cappedByPhaseOut comparison. The tests pin the $100,001/$100,999/$101,001 rounding edges and both zero crossings. One survived: index.html ignoring the MAGI input (magi = 0), because there is no DOM-level test of the wiring. Core logic is well pinned: 3.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (223 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs and index.html. calc.mjs is a small pure module with named constants and an explicit criteria table. Defects: index.html hand-copies the 8 checklist labels instead of rendering them from ELIGIBILITY_CRITERIA, so the page and the module can drift. num() silently turns any non-numeric or negative value into 0, and the page relies on it, so a blank field becomes a confident answer. An unknown filingStatus falls through to the single threshold. Findings HTML is built with innerHTML, but only from module strings and formatted numbers, so it is not an injection risk. A reviewer would accept it with those comments: 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: cap, thresholds, rounding up, zero crossings at $150k/$250k, the joint shared cap, MFS eligible at single thresholds, the senior and tips/overtime MFS exclusions (as I understand 151(d)(5) and 224/225), the 2025 bracket table, disclaimer, no-warranty and privacy (page.test.mjs, no network code). Not backed: the lede says 'This checks every condition', but the VIN-on-the-return requirement and the public-roads/2-wheel vehicle elements are missing. The page cites only the 2026-01-02 proposed regulations while dated 2026-09-24, after the final regulations (T.D. 10054, 2026-09-08). The comparative superlatives ('most calculators get wrong', 'missed most often') have no source. A user acting on 'checks every condition' could file without the VIN: 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked an enrolled agent's 1040 job: one client, a new US-assembled truck, a 1098-VLI showing $6,200 interest, MAGI $118k, single. The tool gives the right capped amount (cap $10,000 - 18 x $200 = $6,400, so all $6,200 is deductible) fast. In the first hour the EA would hit: no VIN capture or reminder for Schedule 1-A; no help splitting qualified from non-qualified interest on a loan that rolled in negative equity or add-ons; refinanced loans not modelled; no MAGI worksheet (AGI plus the 911/931/933 add-backs); no tax-year input, so a 2029 loan or a 2024-originated loan relies on a checkbox; no note that it is available without itemizing. Fine for a consumer estimate, short of preparer use: 2.
evidence.domain: Compared against IRC 163(h)(4) as enacted and T.D. 10054 as summarised by practitioners. Cap, phase-out formula, rounding, joint and MFS treatment and the core exclusions (lease, fleet/commercial, salvage/scrap, first lien, after 2024-12-31, new, US final assembly, GVWR under 14,000 lbs) match. Departures: the VIN requirement is omitted, the final regulations' allocation rules for mixed loans and the refinancing rule are not reflected, the vehicle definition misses the public-roads and 2-wheel elements, and the code comment calls the deduction above-the-line (my understanding is that it is below AGI and open to non-itemizers; stated with some uncertainty). Unsure: whether loans from related parties are excluded by the statute or the regs. I could not verify it this session, so it is not filed. A senior preparer would accept the arithmetic but not the eligibility test as complete: 2.

defects.what: The VIN reporting requirement (no deduction unless the vehicle's VIN is on the return, Schedule 1-A) appears nowhere: not in the 8-item checklist, the findings, the FAQ or the README. The page says it 'checks every condition'. A filer who relies on it can omit the VIN and lose the deduction.

A blank MAGI field is read as $0, and the tool reports the full deduction with an info finding that the interest is 'under ... the phase-out threshold'. A blank interest field likewise gives a silent $0. Confirmed in headless Chrome: blank MAGI with $9,000 interest gives a $9,000 deduction.

Cites only 'Treasury's proposed regulations of 2026-01-02. As of 2026-09-24', but the final regulations (T.D. 10054, 26 CFR 1.163-16) were published 2026-09-08 and take effect 2026-11-09 (per WebSearch summaries; I could not open the Federal Register itself). The interest input gives no guidance on the regs' pro-rata allocation of interest on mixed loans (negative equity, non-qualifying add-ons) or on refinanced debt, which counts up to the balance at refinancing. So 'qualified interest paid' is left to the user.

Unbacked comparative claims: 'the married-filing-separately rule most calculators get wrong' (og:description), 'most people assume works the opposite way', and 'Final assembly location' as the condition 'missed most often'. No file or survey backs them.

The vehicle checklist leaves out the statutory elements 'manufactured primarily for use on public streets, roads, and highways' and 'at least 2 wheels' (which exclude ATVs and golf carts). The RV/camper sentence is asserted without a cited source; I am not certain how the final regs treat campers.

The header comment calls this an 'above-the-line' deduction. As I understand 163(h)(4) and the 63(b)/(d) amendments, it is claimed on Schedule 1-A below AGI and is available to non-itemizers, so it does not reduce AGI. Some practitioner summaries also say 'above the line' loosely; I am not fully certain. The page itself makes no claim either way and never tells the user that it is available without itemizing.
Nothing tests the page wiring: a mutant that ignores the MAGI input (magi = 0) leaves all 41 tests green. page.test.mjs only checks static text and the presence of elements.
An unknown filingStatus silently falls back to the $100,000 threshold, and a non-numeric MAGI (e.g. '1,200,000') becomes 0 through num(). Neither is validated.
The lender statement is called 'Form 1098, where applicable'. The lender information return for this deduction is Form 1098-VLI (sec. 6050AA; a draft form is on irs.gov per WebSearch).

verdict: The arithmetic is right. Five hand recomputations from 163(h)(4) match the shipped code and the live page: the $10,000 per-return cap, the $200 per $1,000-or-portion phase-out over $100k/$200k, MFS at the single threshold, and joint sharing one cap. The tests catch every seeded bug in calc.mjs (5/5). It misses the bar on claims (2). The page says it 'checks every condition' but never mentions that the VIN must be reported on Schedule 1-A. It cites only the January 2026 proposed regulations, although the final regulations (T.D. 10054) came out in September 2026. A blank MAGI silently yields the full deduction. For a preparer it also lacks mixed-loan interest allocation and refinancing (fitness 2, domain 2). Small fixes: add a VIN checklist item or note, refuse a blank MAGI, update the citation. Allocation and refinancing are larger. Statute text could not be fetched this session; see the method notes in checks.
